[32027 Interactive Media | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject introduces you to the core principles and tools of interactive media, widely used across games, the arts, data visualisation, and business. You'll learn to use creative coding to design and develop systems that integrate digital audio, images, animations, and video, aiming to craft rich, engaging user experiences for real-world applications.

[32027 Interactive Media | Learning and teaching activities]
Students prepare for, and participate in, a weekly online lecture of one hour, and a weekly workshop of 2 hours duration facilitated closely in tutorial groups within the large collaborative classrooms.

Students will be provided with readings, online activities and practical work to be completed prior to workshops. Workshops will focus on discussion, clarification, practice and implementation of exercises based on the prepared material.

During workshop sessions, students will collaboratively work on practical design and creative coding activities in their tutorial groups. During this time they will receive coaching and feedback on the specific activities for that week and on their final assignment. Student tutorial groups are expected to bring their assignment work to class in order to receive continuous feedback and coaching throughout the teaching session.

Student achievement of learning outcomes will be assessed in a variety of manners throughout the semester, but there will be presentations at the workshop sessions throughout the semester, and physical attendance is required to complete those presentations and gain marks. There will also be an interactive oral assessment during the assessment period after teaching completes, and physical attendance at this assessment will be required to ensure marks are awarded. Check Canvas for the weighting of this assessment and other details.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32027 Interactive Media | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Apply knowledge of digital sampling, storage and mapping techniques for still images, video, sound and sensor data to make appropriate design choices for interactive media applications. (D.1)
SLO2: Use digital sound, image and video processing algorithms to alter digital media. (D.1)
SLO3: Design and develop interactive media applications which incorporate a range of different interactive components to create effective and engaging user experiences. (C.1)
SLO4: Reflect on the nature of digital media components to devise novel and effective applications and descriptions of interactive media systems. (F.1)
SLO5: Provide creative and critical feedback and ask thoughtful questions of peers in a supportive and constructive manner (E.1)
